question.leadin: The fates of the remnants of both the Holy Roman Empire and post-Napoleonic France were debated in this city.
question.text: Name this Austrian city, site of an 1814-1815 Congress.
question.clue: This event saw Krakow become a free city, and the Earl of Clancarty replaced Castlereagh as England's representative to this event.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about scandals in the French Third Republic.
swap.text: This Austrian reporter's experiences of anti-Semitism in the Dreyfus affair and elsewhere led him to plan the First Zionist Conference.
swap.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

question.text: The Third Defenestration of Prague led to the mobilization of Ferdinand II's armies, who were loyal to this Austrian family that controlled the Holy Roman Empire and Spain. This family's namesake "lip" was a genetic deformity caused by mass inbreeding.
question.clue: Their main branch built an empire which was challenged by nationalistic Croats, Czechs, Poles, and most ominously, Serbs.

swap.leadin: The violation of this 1713 edict led to the War of the Austrian Succession.
swap.text: Name this edict, issued by Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI, which allowed his daughter Maria Theresa to become his successor.
swap.clue: This edict issued by Charles VI permitting Maria Theresa to inherit the throne.

question.text: This first Austro-Hungarian Kaiser und Koenig ruled for 68 years. The assassination of his heir Archduke Ferdinand led to his invasion of Serbia and the start of World War I.
question.clue: This man's reign saw the provinces of Venetia and Lombardy ceded to Italy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Zionist Movement.
swap.text: This man declared that the Dreyfus Affair inspired him to establish the World Zionist Organization that encourages Jewish immigration to Palestine.
swap.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

question.text: Dollfuss' successor, Kurt Schuschnigg, was powerless to stop Hitler's annexation of Austria, an event usually given this name from the German for "connection."
question.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

swap.text: This woman took power in 1740 following the 1713 Pragmatic Sanction. Her son Joseph II attempted reforms like abolishing serfdom, but died at the age of 39.
swap.clue: This leader lost control of Silesia when the Pragmatic Sanction, set up by her father, Charles VI, was violated by Prussia.

question.leadin: Answer these questions relating to Empress Maria Theresa.
question.text: Elector Charles Albert attempted to lay claim to her throne by challenging this doctrine, detailing "legitimate issue."
question.clue: In 1830, Ferdinand VII of Spain relied on one to insure that he would be succeeded by his daughter.

swap.text: In Vienna, one of the first demands of the revolution was the resignation of this man. This Austrian Chancellor used censorship and the secret police to maintain stability in the post-Napoleonic era.

question.text: As emperor of Austria from 1848 to 1916 and king of Hungary from 1867, he did a poor job of, among other things, controlling the ethnic conflicts in his empire.
question.clue: A prince from Liechtenstein with this name protected his country's neutrality during World War II. The wife of an earlier leader with this name, Elisabeth, was stabbed to death by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni.

swap.text: Becoming the ruler of and following the Revolutions of 1848, he led his country into WWI before dying in 1916.
swap.answer: Franz-Josef I or Francis Joseph I

question.leadin: Answer the following about Habsburgs who met tragic ends within a span of only 25 years.
question.text: The marriage of Elisabeth and Franz Joseph was damaged after their only son, a crown prince of this name, committed suicide with his lover at Mayerling. This is also the name of the first Habsburg king of Germany.
question.answerHtml: Rudolf [accept Rudolf I or Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria]
question.clue: A ruler of this name greatly increased his territories after he defeated Ottokar II at the Battle of Marchfeld.

swap.leadin: A minister of this ruler freed peasants from their compulsory robota labor by breaking up church-owned estates in a process known as "Raabization."
swap.text: Name this ruler who also introduced one of the first compulsory public school systems. This ruler was officially designated as heir in an edict issued by Charles VI.
swap.answerHtml: Maria Theresa of Austria [or Maria Theresa Walburgia Amalia Christina]
swap.clue: Wenzel Kaunitz failed to persuade this monarch to not reclaim Silesia from Frederick II.

question.text: Your belief in Central Power unity was probably shattered following this affair late in the war. In this affair, Clemenceau published Emperor Charles I's correspondence with the namesake person asking for peace with the Allies.

swap.text: This Chancellor capitalized on the "self-elimination" of parliament in 1933 to assume emergency powers and ban all parties except his Fatherland Front, kicking off the civil war between Austrofascists and Austromarxists.
swap.clue: This dictator absorbed the Heimwehr of Prince Starhemberg to establish the Fatherland Front, but was assassinated by Otto Planetta during the July Putsch.

question.leadin: Philip V's initiation of the War of the Quadruple Alliance relied on Austria, and especially this victor at Oudenarde and Malplaquet, being preoccupied with the Ottomans.
question.text: Name this likely gay general who teamed up with the Duke of Marlborough during the War of the Spanish Succession.
question.clue: He fought several battles in Italy, including the Battle of Chiari and his assault on the fortress of Cremona.

swap.text: In this 1805 treaty that paved the way for the Confederation of the Rhine, Francis II of Austria was forced to pay 40 million gold francs to France. Austria did gain Salzburg in this treaty, though.
swap.clue: This treaty granted the title of king to the Electors of Bavaria, Wurtumberg and Baden and would effectively result in the creation of the Confederation of the Rhine.

question.text: For years, Haider was governor of this southern Austrian state, where he attracted controversy for his adversarial stance toward its native Slovene population.

swap.text: Frederick was less enthused about this treaty, through which Louis XIV forced him to give up his Pomeranian holdings won at Fehrbellin in the Scanian War. Karl Renner was also forced by the French to sign a treaty by this name in the wake of the Battle of Vittorio Veneto.
swap.answerHtml: Treaty of Saint Germain-en-Laye [do not accept or prompt on “Saint-Germain”]
